title: Formulary Benefit Specialty Transition Supplies: Review Allowance for a Paired Biosimilar that Needs Prior Authorization
content:
Under the Formulary Benefit, a specialty transition supply carries a biosimilar review allowance when the drug is paired with a preferred biosimilar that needs prior authorization. The allowance gives the member time for that biosimilar's review. Its size depends on three records: the pairing in the member's Specialty Pharmacy Program, the prior-authorization list of the member's review package under the Utilization Management Program, and the member's authorization history for the biosimilar.

## Allowance clause

- **(a)** The Specialty Pharmacy Program pairs the drug with a preferred biosimilar, that biosimilar is on the prior-authorization list of the member's review package, and no authorization for it has ever been granted to the member. The package's standard review time in days is added. That is the package's standard decision hours divided by twenty-four.
- **(b)** The program pairs the drug with that biosimilar, it is on that list, an authorization for it was granted to the member, and the latest such authorization expired before the handling date. The package's urgent review time in days is added. That is the package's urgent decision hours divided by twenty-four.
- **(c)** In every other case, no biosimilar review allowance is added.

The allowance is added to the supply's dose-cycle days. Only after that is the supply held between zero and the formulary's maximum days supply for one transition fill and taken in whole days.

## Truth table

| Paired | On the package's prior-authorization list | Authorizations for the biosimilar ever granted | Latest one expired before the handling date | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | none | not applicable | standard decision hours divided by 24 |
| yes | yes | one or more | yes | urgent decision hours divided by 24 |
| yes | yes | one or more | no (still in force on the handling date) | none |
| yes | no | any | any | none |
| no | any | any | any | none |

*Hypothetical package hours.* Suppose a review package decides standard reviews in 72 hours and urgent reviews in 24 hours. A member who has never been authorized for the paired biosimilar receives 3 days. A member whose authorization expired the week before the handling date receives 1 day. A member whose authorization runs past the handling date receives nothing. With standard hours of 36, the allowance would be 1.5 days, and the whole-day rounding applies only to the finished supply.
